Senses.PreferredTarget: the ancient buddha passed away long ago
AlternateTargets: the old buddha has long since gone
Senses.Note: Two witnesses preserve Yanguan’s bottle-case answer; four later masters independently redeploy the exact sentence.

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Yanguan Qi’an’s sentence that the ancient buddha passed away long ago first answers a repeated question after a water bottle is moved out and back. Later masters lift the sentence out of that exchange and use it as a fresh answer or hall verdict.
EvidenceBody: Yanguan gives the sentence only after the bottle has been brought and replaced. Zhanran Yuancheng gives it when an official tries to continue after asking for the “golden needle”; Zhenxie Qingliao uses it after warning that a raised eyebrow is already a miss; Cishou Huaishen repeats it as his own closing answer; and Wuming Huijing raises his staff and asks whether the assembly wants another ladle of foul water.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: A statement about an ancient buddha becomes both the decisive answer in Yanguan’s public interview and a reusable sentence delivered in later halls.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The corpus does not make “ancient buddha” a separate person here or gloss one hidden intention shared by every later use.

ComparedThings: later masters’ redeployment of the same sentence
DifferentThingTest.Reason: All witnesses use the same complete assertion; changed occasions and appraisals do not create a different referent.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: The aliases retrieve the same complete answer through natural English variants for ancient/old and gone/departed.

ModifierControls.reason: No material or color modifier occurs in the headword.

FamilyControls.reason: Two recensions establish the original bottle exchange; later exact headword-bearing uses, rather than further duplicate recensions, supply the remaining depth.
